outgoing.name: Carolus Linnaeus
outgoing.excerpt: Esox (Linnaeus, 1758) is a genus of freshwater fish, the only member of the pike family (family Esocidae) of order Esociformes.

outgoing.name: Latin
outgoing.excerpt: Pliny uses the Latin form esox in reference to a large fish in the Rhine normally identified with lax (salmon).

outgoing.name: NATO
outgoing.excerpt: In addition, the Soviet submarines known to NATO as the Victor III class were called the Shchuka (Щука, "pike") class, in Russian.

outgoing.name: North America
outgoing.excerpt: The pike species are native to the Palearctic and Nearctic ecozones, ranging across northern North America and from Western Europe to Siberia in Eurasia.

outgoing.name: Old English language
outgoing.excerpt: The English common name "pike" is an apparent shortening of "pike-fish", in reference to its pointed head, Old English píc originally referring to a pickaxe.
